newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt minister hears Sudan opposition goals.
newsitem.headline: Egypt minister hears Sudan opposition goals.

text.p: Sudanese opposition leader Sadeq al-Mahdi on Monday met Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa and explained the opposition's goal to get rid of the Khartoum government.
Mahdi said Moussa was understanding of "the aspirations of the Sudanese people and the means they are taking to achieve their legitimate goals".

Mahdi, prime minister of Sudan when Omar Hassan al-Bashir seized power in a bloodless coup in 1989, fled to Eritrea earlier this month saying he wanted to change the government with a minimum of bloodshed.
"Most Sudanese reject the ruling regime and want to get rid of it as soon as possible, with minimum bloodshed and loss of lives," Mahdi told reporters after his meeting with Moussa.
"The Sudanese opposition agrees with this goal -- overthrowing the Sudanese regime," he added.
Mahdi's talks with Moussa came on the heels of a meeting between President Hosni Mubarak and Mohammed Osman al-Mirghani, another Sudanese opposition leader.

Mirghani, who is the chairman of the opposition National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in exile, arrived in Cairo on Sunday from Saudi Arabia at the invitation of the Egyptian government. He did not speak to reporters after his meeting with Mubarak.

Mirghani and Mahdi lead the two big traditional parties in northern Sudan, the Democratic Unionists and the Umma Party. Both parties are in the NDA, along with the southern rebels of the Sudan People's Liberation Movement.
The Sudanese opposition in exile has offices in Cairo but its contacts with the Egyptian government are rarely publicised.

Relations between Egypt and Sudan have deteriorated over the past few years with Cairo implicating Khartoum in an attempted assassination of Mubarak in Ethiopia in June 1995 and of sheltering Moslem militants bent on overthrowing the Egyptian government.
Sudan has denied the charges and has lashed out at Egypt for allowing the Sudanese opposition to operate in Cairo.
